To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the spoilage of sous vide cooked salmon stored under chilling conditions was mainly due to sensory deterioration and that this deterioration was mainly caused by loss of odor and flavor, discoloration, and softness.

SV processing prevents the growth of aerobic, and anaerobic, psychrotrophic microorganisms, lactic acid, and molds and yeasts, and Enterobactericeae, and that SV cooked salmon suffers sensory deterioration during its storage at refrigerated temperatures.

the SV cooking process prevented the growth of all microorganisms studied, but it could not prevent the sensory deterioration of cooked salmon during refrigerated storage, which occurred in a few days.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the spoilage of SV cooked salmon stored under cold chain.
the development of a new technology for the processing of cooked salmon, which can be stored for up to 10 weeks under refrigeration.
the spoilage of SV cooked salmon stored under catering conditions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

SV cooked salmon stored at 2 ºC for 0 to 10 weeks is microbiologically safe and stable in terms of physical—chemical parameters, but is highly perishable and of low acceptability due to its sensory spoilage.
SV cooked salmon is a highly perishable food, with a very short shelf life, which should be consumed immediately after cooking.
SV processing of salmon fillets at 80 °C for 45 min, quickly chilling, packaging and storage under refrigeration at 2 ° C for 5 or 6 weeks is a good alternative for catering use.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the sensory spoilage of SV cooked salmon is mainly caused by the development of cooked salmon off—odors and off—flavors and that the microbiological and physical-chemical spoilage is not relevant in this case.
SV cooking of salmon is an excellent preservation technique, since it prevents microbiological spoilage and reduces the risk of chemical and physical spoilage.
SV processing is not a panacea, and the shelf-life of SV cooked salmon depends on the quality of the raw product and the storage conditions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SV processing is a very effective way to prevent the microbial spoilage of cooked salmon, but the sensory spoilage of SV cooked salmon may be faster than the microbial spoilage.
the SV cooked salmon is highly perishable, and its refrigerated storage life is very short (less than one week) and should be used within 5–6 days after cooking.
the sensory shelf life is shorter than that predicted by microbiological and physical-chemical spoilage indicators.
